properties.headline: Ground sinking along the northern Delta coast
properties.subtitle: Coastal farmland
properties.summary: The radar shows this land sinking a little more with every pass. The drop is steady, not sudden, so it isn't from a single event.
causes: Groundwater pumped for farms and towns
properties.why_it_matters: Low fields near the coast become more exposed to seawater and flooding.
properties.next_step: Compare with groundwater and land-use records for this area.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured the ground along this stretch of coast dropping by about 6.7 millimetres, which is a rate of roughly 8 millimetres per year.

The sinking is smooth and continuous. A sudden event such as an earthquake would show up as a sharp step, and there is none here. That pattern is consistent with slow settling of soft delta soil, possibly made faster by groundwater being pumped out.

Why it matters: the Delta is already very flat. Even small drops can let seawater reach farmland more easily. This is an early signal to check against groundwater and land-use records, not a confirmed cause.

properties.headline: Soil moisture shifting across mid-Delta farmland
properties.subtitle: Irrigated cropland
properties.confidence_note: Seasonal irrigation may explain part of this
properties.summary: Radar signals from these fields rise and fall in rhythm with the season. Overall the soil looks wetter than at the start of the year.
causes: Irrigation and flooding of fields for crops
Seasonal rainfall and rising water tables
properties.why_it_matters: Wetter soil can affect crop health and how salty the land becomes over time.
properties.next_step: Compare with crop calendars and irrigation schedules.
properties.explanation:
Radar is sensitive to water in the soil: wetter ground reflects the signal differently. Across this region the signal grew steadily stronger through the year, with a small seasonal wobble.

That is consistent with a combination of irrigation and a higher water table. Farmers flood fields on a schedule, so some of the movement is simply the farming calendar.

This is a trend worth watching rather than a warning. If moisture keeps rising, soil salinity could become a concern.

properties.headline: Rapid ground change at new city construction east of Cairo
properties.subtitle: New urban development
properties.summary: This patch of desert became much brighter on radar around mid-year. That sudden jump is the signature of buildings and roads appearing.
causes: New buildings and roads replacing open desert
properties.why_it_matters: Fast urban growth changes water demand, traffic and how the ground behaves.
properties.next_step: Confirm with high-resolution optical imagery.
properties.explanation:
Hard, angular surfaces like walls and roofs bounce radar straight back to the satellite, so built-up areas look very bright. Here the signal jumped by about 3.8 decibels over just a few passes.

A sudden step like this is different from slow natural change. It is consistent with construction starting across a large area.

A photo from another satellite could confirm what is being built.

properties.headline: Water edges moving around the north-eastern lagoon
properties.subtitle: Coastal lagoon
properties.confidence_note: Tides and seasons both play a part
properties.summary: Open water is smooth and looks dark to radar, so the edge of the lagoon is easy to trace. Over the year that edge crept inland in places.
causes: Sea level and tides pushing into the lagoon
properties.why_it_matters: Moving shorelines affect fishing, nearby farms and wetland wildlife.
properties.next_step: Compare with tide and rainfall records.
properties.explanation:
Calm water reflects radar away from the satellite, so it appears dark. That makes shorelines very clear in radar images.

Over the observation period the lagoon edge shifted inland by up to about 120 metres in some places.

The movement is consistent with seasonal water-level changes and possibly the sea pushing in. More data would show whether this is a cycle or a lasting trend.

properties.headline: Lake shoreline shifting with water levels
properties.subtitle: Reservoir shoreline
properties.summary: The lake edge has pulled back from where it was in January, which suggests the water level has dropped.
causes: Less inflow during the dry months
properties.why_it_matters: Lake levels affect water supply, power generation and farming downstream.
properties.next_step: Compare with dam operation records.
properties.explanation:
The shoreline of this large reservoir is easy to track because water looks dark on radar. Over the year the edge retreated, which means the water level fell by an estimated 1.8 metres.

Reservoir levels naturally rise and fall with the seasons and with how much water is released. This pattern is consistent with a normal drawdown, though operation records would be needed to be sure.

properties.headline: New farmland expanding west of the lake
properties.subtitle: Desert reclamation
properties.summary: Patches of desert west of the lake are changing in a way that fits new crops being planted and irrigated.
causes: Pumped water feeding reclaimed desert land
properties.why_it_matters: Large new farms use a lot of water and change the local landscape.
properties.next_step: Check with optical imagery to confirm the crops.
properties.explanation:
Growing plants and wet soil change how radar bounces back. West of the lake, signals in several round patches shifted in a way consistent with irrigated crops.

Radar only sees plants indirectly, so confidence is lower here. An optical satellite image would show green fields clearly and confirm it.

properties.headline: Mexico City ground keeps sinking
properties.subtitle: Dense urban area
properties.summary: The city sits on an old lake bed. The radar shows the ground dropping steadily, fastest in the south-east.
causes: Groundwater pumped from the clay beneath the city
properties.why_it_matters: Uneven sinking can crack pipes, roads and buildings.
properties.next_step: Compare with groundwater pumping records.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of -30 mm per year across about 220 km².

This pattern is consistent with groundwater pumped from the clay beneath the city, and possibly soft lake-bed soil compacting. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Uneven sinking can crack pipes, roads and buildings.

properties.headline: Northern Jakarta sinking toward the sea
properties.subtitle: Coastal megacity

causes: Groundwater extraction for homes and industry
Weight of buildings on soft coastal soil
properties.why_it_matters: Low coastal land floods more easily when it sinks.
properties.next_step: Compare with well-extraction and tide records.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of -60 mm per year across about 90 km².

This pattern is consistent with groundwater extraction for homes and industry, and possibly weight of buildings on soft coastal soil. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Low coastal land floods more easily when it sinks.

properties.headline: California farmland sinking as groundwater drops
properties.subtitle: Irrigated farmland
properties.summary: A wide strip of farmland is dropping, with the fastest sinking in the middle of the valley.
causes: Heavy groundwater pumping during dry spells
properties.why_it_matters: Sinking can damage canals and permanently reduce water storage.
properties.next_step: Compare with well-level and canal data.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of -100 mm per year across about 1400 km².

This pattern is consistent with heavy groundwater pumping during dry spells, and possibly compaction of clay layers underground. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Sinking can damage canals and permanently reduce water storage.

properties.headline: Ground slowly settling around the Venice lagoon
properties.subtitle: Historic lagoon city
properties.summary: The ground here is sinking only slightly, but it adds up in a place that already floods.
properties.why_it_matters: Even millimetres matter where streets are close to sea level.
properties.next_step: Compare with tide-gauge records.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of -2 mm per year across about 160 km².

This pattern is consistent with natural settling of lagoon sediments, and possibly past groundwater use. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Even millimetres matter where streets are close to sea level.

properties.headline: Mekong Delta coast sinking
properties.subtitle: River delta farmland
properties.summary: Much of the delta is dropping a little each year, more than the sea is rising.
causes: Groundwater pumping for rice and shrimp farms
Less river sediment reaching the delta
properties.why_it_matters: A sinking delta lets salt water reach farmland and drinking water.
properties.next_step: Compare with groundwater and sediment records.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of -18 mm per year across about 600 km².

This pattern is consistent with groundwater pumping for rice and shrimp farms, and possibly less river sediment reaching the delta. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: A sinking delta lets salt water reach farmland and drinking water.

properties.headline: Ground rising near an Iceland volcano
properties.subtitle: Volcanic area
properties.summary: The ground is swelling slowly upward, a sign that something is moving underneath.
causes: Pressure changes in hot underground water
properties.why_it_matters: Ground swelling is one of the signs scientists watch before an eruption.
properties.next_step: Share with the local geology and monitoring office.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of +35 mm per year across about 70 km².

This pattern is consistent with magma collecting underground, and possibly pressure changes in hot underground water. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Ground swelling is one of the signs scientists watch before an eruption.

properties.headline: Reservoir shoreline retreating at Lake Mead
properties.subtitle: Desert reservoir
properties.summary: The edge of the lake has pulled back, leaving pale bands of dry shoreline.
causes: Less river inflow in dry years
properties.why_it_matters: Lower levels affect drinking water and hydropower.
properties.next_step: Compare with reservoir operation data.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured water level change of -3.4 m across about 250 km².

This pattern is consistent with less river inflow in dry years, and possibly high demand for water downstream. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Lower levels affect drinking water and hydropower.

properties.headline: Lake Chad water edge shifting
properties.subtitle: Seasonal lake
properties.summary: The open-water area is larger than at the start of the year, though it changes with the seasons.
properties.why_it_matters: Millions of people rely on this shallow lake for fishing and farming.
properties.next_step: Compare with rainfall and river-flow records.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured water area of +6 % growth across about 900 km².

This pattern is consistent with seasonal rains and river flow, and possibly natural year-to-year swings. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Millions of people rely on this shallow lake for fishing and farming.

properties.headline: Dried seabed expanding around the Aral Sea
properties.subtitle: Former inland sea
properties.summary: The remaining water is shrinking, leaving more dry seabed.
properties.why_it_matters: Dry seabed can blow dust and salt across nearby farmland.
properties.next_step: Compare with river diversion records.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured water area of -4 % shrink across about 1200 km².

This pattern is consistent with river water diverted for crops, and possibly low rainfall. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Dry seabed can blow dust and salt across nearby farmland.

causes: Forest cleared for farms and pasture
Fire damage in the dry season
properties.why_it_matters: Forest loss affects wildlife, rainfall and stored carbon.
properties.next_step: Confirm with optical imagery.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured forest signal of -12 % change across about 1800 km².

This pattern is consistent with forest cleared for farms and pasture, and possibly fire damage in the dry season. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Forest loss affects wildlife, rainfall and stored carbon.

properties.headline: New districts rising around Dubai
properties.subtitle: Coastal urban growth
properties.summary: Patches of open desert are getting brighter on radar, as new buildings and roads appear.
causes: New buildings and roads on open desert
properties.why_it_matters: Fast growth changes water demand and how the ground behaves.
properties.next_step: Confirm with high-resolution optical imagery.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured radar brightness of +2.1 dB increase across about 140 km².

This pattern is consistent with new buildings and roads on open desert, and possibly land reclaimed along the coast. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Fast growth changes water demand and how the ground behaves.

properties.headline: Soil getting wetter across the Ganges plain
properties.subtitle: Irrigated cropland
properties.summary: Soil across a wide area looks wetter than in January, with a clear seasonal rhythm.
properties.why_it_matters: Wetter soil affects crop planting and flood risk.
properties.next_step: Compare with rainfall and crop calendars.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured soil moisture of +8 % change across about 2600 km².

This pattern is consistent with monsoon rain and irrigation, and possibly rising shallow water tables. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Wetter soil affects crop planting and flood risk.

properties.headline: Stable ground across the western desert
properties.subtitle: Open desert
properties.summary: The radar sees almost no movement here. That is useful: it shows the method is steady.
causes: Hard, dry ground with little water
properties.why_it_matters: Calm areas help confirm that changes elsewhere are real.
properties.next_step: Keep as a reference area.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of +0.4 mm per year across about 4000 km².

This pattern is consistent with hard, dry ground with little water, and possibly no major human activity. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: Calm areas help confirm that changes elsewhere are real.

properties.headline: Stable ground across the Canadian Shield
properties.subtitle: Ancient bedrock
properties.summary: This old rock is steady. It is rising extremely slowly after the ice age.
properties.why_it_matters: A good reference area for measuring change elsewhere.
properties.next_step: Keep as a reference area.
properties.explanation:
Between January and October the radar measured ground movement of +0.6 mm per year across about 5200 km².

This pattern is consistent with slow rebound after ice-age glaciers, and possibly very little human activity. This does not prove a cause.

Why it matters: A good reference area for measuring change elsewhere.
